questions.title: Most Registered General Aviation Aircraft
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most registered general aviation aircraft.
questions.disclaimer: Civil aircraft registered to owners with in-state addresses. Excludes commercial airline fleets registered at corporate HQ addresses. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: FAA — US Civil Airmen and Aircraft Statistics

questions.title: Highest Share of Structurally Deficient Bridges
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the highest percentage of bridges rated in poor (structurally deficient) condition.
questions.disclaimer: Share of a state's public road bridges rated in Poor condition under the FHWA NBI (formerly 'structurally deficient'). Includes Washington DC.

questions.title: Most High-Hazard-Potential Dams
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most dams rated High-Hazard-Potential in the National Inventory of Dams.
questions.disclaimer: High-Hazard-Potential dams are those whose failure would likely cause loss of human life, regardless of dam size or current condition. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Army Corps of Engineers — National Inventory of Dams (NID)

questions.title: Highest Public Transit Ridership per Capita
questions.prompt: Name the US states (including DC) with the highest annual public transit ridership per resident.
questions.disclaimer: Unlinked passenger trips per resident, all reported transit modes. State totals derived from NTD agency reports. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: FTA — National Transit Database (Annual Unlinked Passenger Trips per capita)

questions.title: Highest Average Gasoline Price
questions.prompt: Name the US states (including DC) with the highest average price for a gallon of regular unleaded gasoline.
questions.disclaimer: State average price per gallon of regular unleaded. Prices reflect state-level taxes, transportation costs, and fuel-blend requirements. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: AAA — Daily Fuel Gauge Report (State Averages)

questions.title: Most Freight Rail Miles
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most miles of freight railroad track.
questions.disclaimer: Route miles of freight railroad (Class I, regional, and short line), not track miles. Route mileage counts a rail corridor once regardless of parallel tracks. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: BTS / AAR — State Rankings by Freight Rail Route Miles

questions.title: Most National Historic Landmarks
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most designated National Historic Landmarks.
questions.disclaimer: Landmarks that span more than one state are counted once for each state they touch, so state totals include a small amount of double-counting. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: National Park Service — National Historic Landmarks Program (per-state totals compiled on Wikipedia)

questions.title: Most National Natural Landmarks
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most designated National Natural Landmarks.
questions.disclaimer: A handful of landmarks span two states and are counted for each state they touch. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: National Park Service — National Natural Landmarks Program (per-state totals on Wikipedia)

questions.title: Highest Peak Inside a National Park
questions.prompt: Rank US states by the elevation of the highest named summit located inside a National Park within the state.
questions.disclaimer: Only formally designated National Parks are counted (not National Monuments, Preserves, or Recreation Areas). Multi-state parks are credited to the state where the highest in-park summit lies. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

source.name: National Park Service — park summit data (elevations from USGS and NPS park pages)

questions.title: Largest Fully In-State Lake by Surface Area
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the largest single lake located entirely within the state's borders (by surface area).
questions.disclaimer: Excludes lakes that cross state or international borders (Great Lakes, Lake Champlain, Lake Tahoe, Lake Powell, Kentucky Lake, Toledo Bend, Lake Mead, etc.). Great Salt Lake and Salton Sea are included despite being saline. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: Wikipedia — List of largest lakes of the United States by area (compiled from USGS and state sources)

questions.title: Highest Forest Cover Percentage
questions.prompt: Rank US states by percent of the state's land area covered by forest.
questions.disclaimer: Percent forested is computed on land area only (excluding inland water). US territories such as American Samoa are excluded from this state-only ranking. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: USDA Forest Service — Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) 2016 Business Report

questions.title: Most Counties or County Equivalents
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most counties (or county-equivalent divisions such as parishes and independent cities).
questions.disclaimer: County-equivalent divisions (parishes, boroughs, and independent cities) are counted alongside counties. States that combine a county and an independent city count both. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — Counties and County Equivalents (via Wikipedia list)

questions.title: Greatest Elevation Range Within a State
questions.prompt: Rank US states by the difference between the state's highest point and its lowest point.
questions.disclaimer: Range equals the state high point minus the state low point. States with sub-sea-level low points get a small boost in range from the negative minimum. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: USGS — state high-point and low-point data (compiled on Wikipedia)

questions.title: Largest State Fair by Attendance
questions.prompt: Rank US states by the annual attendance of their state fair.
questions.disclaimer: Only official single-state fairs are counted here; regional/multi-state exhibitions (such as the New England Big E) are excluded. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: Wikipedia — State fair (attendance figures cited from each fair's official reports)

questions.title: Most Total Forest Land Area (Acres)
questions.prompt: Rank US states by total forest land area, in acres.
questions.disclaimer: Measures absolute forest land in acres, not percent of state forested. FIA counts all forested land (public, private, and tribal). Includes Washington DC.

source.name: USDA Forest Service — Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) state totals

questions.title: Most Wilderness Acreage
questions.prompt: Rank US states by the number of acres protected under the National Wilderness Preservation System.
questions.disclaimer: Wilderness areas that cross state boundaries have their acreage split by state. Six states (Connecticut, Delaware, Iowa, Kansas, Maryland, Rhode Island) contain no designated wilderness. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

source.name: National Wilderness Preservation System — Wilderness.net & Wikipedia state totals
